source_title: Adjusting Imports of Unmanned Aircraft Systems and Unmanned Aircraft Systems Components into the United States
banner_title: U.S. slaps 25%-100% drone tariffs — domestic makers gain protection
banner_title_zh: 美国对无人机加征25%-100%关税——本土制造商获保护
summary: The United States will impose 25%-100% Section 232 tariffs on specified drones, docking stations and critical components beginning September 3, with additional component duties following after 180 days. The action protects domestic drone manufacturing but raises near-term costs for import-dependent producers and commercial operators.
summary_zh: 美国将从9月3日起依据“232条款”对特定无人机、停机坪及关键部件征收25%-100%的关税，其他部件关税将在180天后生效。该措施保护美国本土无人机制造业，但会提高依赖进口的制造商和商业运营商的近期成本。
analysis:
The proclamation applies a 100% tariff to specified drones weighing more than 25 kilograms, drones integrating thermal imagers, docking stations and certain critical components. Specified drones weighing 25 kilograms or less face a 25% tariff, while another group of components will face a 25% duty after a 180-day transition.

The direct transmission mechanism is a sharp increase in the landed cost of covered foreign systems, improving the competitive position and pricing power of U.S.-based drone manufacturers. At the same time, many domestic assemblers still depend on imported motors, batteries, electronic speed controllers and other components, so the policy may pressure margins until local supply expands.

The Commerce Secretary can add components to the tariff scope and establish preferential treatment for companies committing to new U.S. production. The key uncertainty is the omitted annex-level product coverage and how broadly exemptions or onshoring incentives will reduce effective tariff rates.
